question.text: A rock is projected straight up into the air. As it passes through half of its highest elevation, it travels at a speed of 10 ms⁻¹. Determine the peak elevation achieved by the rock. (Take g = 10 ms⁻²)
conditions: speed at half of maximum height is 10 ms⁻¹
speed at maximum height is 0 ms⁻¹

solution.approach: Use the equation of motion between the launch point and the halfway point, with speed zero at maximum height, to eliminate the initial speed and find the maximum height.

steps.text: Let u be the launch speed and H the maximum height. Since the speed is zero at the top, u² = 2gH.
Apply v² = u² − 2g(H/2) at the halfway point, where the speed is 10 ms⁻¹.
Solve for H using g = 10 ms⁻².

common_mistakes.text: Assuming the speed falls in proportion to height, so the launch speed is twice 10 ms⁻¹, gives H = 20²/(2×10) = 20 m.
